question: What color and dimensional limits apply to crosswalk markings, including transverse crosswalk lines?
model_answer: Direct Answer: Crosswalk markings must be white, and transverse lines used to establish a crosswalk must be between 6 and 24 inches wide. The minimum marked crosswalk width is 6 feet, increasing to 8 feet at non-intersection crosswalks where the posted speed limit is 40 mph or greater. High-visibility designs (longitudinal bar, ladder, bar pair) with their own dimensional ranges are permitted where added conspicuity is desired. Standards (mandatory): - "The transverse lines used to establish the limits of the ladder crosswalk shall not be less than 6 inches or greater than 24 inches in width." - Per Section 3C.03 shown on the attached page: "Crosswalk markings shall be white. When used, transverse lines shall not be less than 6 inches or greater than 24 inches in width," and "Except as provided in Paragraph 6 of this Section, the minimum width of a marked crosswalk shall be 6 feet. At a non-intersection crosswalk where the posted speed limit is 40 mph or greater, the minimum width of the crosswalk shall be 8 feet." [Image 5] Guidance (recommended): - Transverse line crosswalk markings should be limited to locations controlled by traffic control signals or on approaches controlled by STOP or YIELD signs. - To provide contrast with aesthetic surface treatments, a gap of at least one-half the width of the white transverse line, but not less than 6 inches, should be used between the white crosswalk lines and the aesthetic treatment (unmarked pavement or a black contrast line). Options (permitted): - High-visibility crosswalk markings may be used where additional conspicuity is desired for a crosswalk over transverse line crosswalk markings. Visual evidence: - [Image 5] Page 631 shows Section 3C.03 and Figure 3C-1, stating crosswalk markings shall be white, transverse lines 6–24 inches wide, 6 ft minimum crosswalk width (8 ft at non-intersection crosswalks with posted speeds of 40 mph or greater), and giving dimensional ranges for longitudinal bar (12–24 inches wide bars), ladder, and bar pair (8–12 inches per bar) designs. - [Image 6] Page 632 shows Sections 3C.04 and 3C.05, describing transverse line and high-visibility crosswalk designs and requiring at least three individual longitudinal elements for a high-visibility crosswalk. - [Image 1] Figure 3C-2 illustrates example crosswalk markings at an intersection with an exclusive pedestrian phase, noting high-visibility crosswalks can be used around the perimeter of the intersection. - [Image 8] Page 664 (Section 3H.03) shows the contrast-gap guidance between white crosswalk lines and aesthetic surface treatments (at least half the transverse line width, not less than 6 inches). - [Image 4] Figure 3B-27 shows white markings dimensioned in the vicinity of a crosswalk/speed table area (12-inch white markings), consistent with white marking requirements. Citations: - Section 3C.07 Standard §4 (p.592) - Section 3C.04 Guidance §1 (p.591) - Section 3C.05 Option §1 (p.591) - Section 3H.03 Guidance §11 (p.623) - Section 3C.01 Support §1 (p.589) - Figure 3C-2 (p.593) - Figure 3B-27 (p.586) - Page 631 - Page 632 - Page 664
gold_answer: Crosswalk markings must be white. Where transverse lines are used, each line must be at least 6 inches and no more than 24 inches wide. Except for certain ramp-terminal cases, the marked crosswalk should be at least 6 feet wide.
